ety.text: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit आशिन् (āśin). By surface analysis, आश (āś) + -ई (-ī).

s.g: a single group or a group having a specific purpose, a detachment
a male given name, Ivan, from Russian

ety.text: Borrowed from Russian Ива́н (Iván). Doublet of जॉन (jŏn) and यूहन्ना (yūhannā).

s.g: A hole or pit for catching elephants, tigers etc.

ety.text: Semi-learned borrowing from Sanskrit कणिक (kaṇika). Doublet of कणिक (kaṇik) and कनिक (kanik).

s.g: a female given name, Kanak, from Sanskrit
to utter a shrill cry (as a peacock or cuckoo), scream

ety.text: Inherited from Prakrit कुक्कइ (kukkaï), which is onomatopoeic. Compare Sanskrit कुहुरव (kuhurava), कोकिल (kokila), कुहक्क (kuhakka).

s.g: to wind, wind up (as a watch)

ety.text: Verbalized from कूका (kūkā, “wound up”), from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *कुक्क (kukka), from older *क्रुक्न (*krukna), a -न (-na) variant of Sanskrit क्रुक्त (krukta), the past participle of the root क्रुञ्च् (kruñc).

s.g: religious act or ceremony, pious act, a duty

x: नदी में बहुत सारे चिकने पत्थर हैं।

ety.text: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀘𑀺𑀓𑁆𑀓𑀡 (cikkaṇa) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-).

x: चेतना जब चौकन्नी हो जाती है तो उसे चारों तरफ़ मामूलियत की फीकी चमक के सिवा कुछ नज़र नहीं आता।
इसकी दृष्टि तेज़ और चौकन्नी होती है।

ety.text: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀘𑀉𑀓𑁆𑀓𑀡𑁆𑀡 (caükkaṇṇa) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-), from Sanskrit चतुष्कर्ण (catuṣkarṇa, “four-eared; having four ears”).
Borrowed from Classical Persian تَابُوت (tābūt), in turn borrowed from Arabic تَابُوت (tābūt).

x: चोट मुझको अभी भी दर्द कर रही है।

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian درد زه (dard-i zih).

s.g: Dvitiya, the second day of a paksha (half of a lunar month)

ety.text: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀤𑀼𑀇𑀚𑁆𑀚 (duijja), from Sanskrit द्वितीय (dvitī́ya, “second”), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *dwitíyas, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dwitíyas, from Proto-Indo-European *dwitíyos, from *dwi- (“two, apart”). Doublet of दूजा (dūjā) and दूसरा (dūsrā).
Borrowed from Classical Persian پارچه (pārča), from پاره (pāra) + diminutive suffix چه (ča).

x: इस लड़की के पास बहुत लंबे-लंबे बाल हैं।

ety.text: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀯𑀸𑀮 (vāla), from Sanskrit वाल (vāla). Cognate with Assamese বাল (bal, “pubic hair”).
Borrowed from Classical Persian بال (bāl), from Middle Persian b’lk’ (bālag, “wing”).

x: मिट्टी के बासन को इतनी सकत कहाँ जो अपने कुम्हार के करतब कुछ ताड़ सके।

ety.text: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀯𑁄𑀚𑁆𑀛 (vojjha), from Sanskrit वह्य (vahya), from Proto-Indo-European *wóǵʰ-yo-s (“fit to be carried”), from *weǵʰ- (“to carry, draw”).
Borrowed from Classical Persian مخمل (maxmal), from Arabic مُخْمَل (muḵmal). Compare Gujarati મખમલ (makhmal), Punjabi ਮਖਮਲ (makhmal).

s.g: alternative spelling of मस्तिष्क स्तंभ (mastiṣk stambh, “brainstem”)

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian یَقِین (yaqīn), from Arabic يَقِين (yaqīn).

x: मुझे यक़ीन नहीं हो रहा है!

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian یَقِین (yaqīn), from Arabic يَقِين (yaqīn).

Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀲𑀁𑀩𑀼𑀚𑁆𑀛𑀤𑀺 (saṃbujjhadi), from Sanskrit सम्बुध्यते (sambudhyate). Cognate with Bengali সমঝা (śomojha), Punjabi ਸਮਝਣਾ (samjhaṇā) / سَمجھݨا (samjhṇā), Gujarati સમજવું (samajvũ), Marathi समजणे (samajṇe).

s.g: a female given name, Sushma, from Sanskrit

ety.text: From Proto-New Indo-Aryan *हग्गइ (haggaï). See there for more.
